events.objective: Establish whether the payment failures are real and where. Determine the onset time of customer-visible failure (look for incident-like signals ~11:45-12:30Z, ~40 tickets in the last ~15 min before 12:32). Check payment-service's full metric set, not just error_rate: latency percentiles (p95/p99), timeout counts, request rate/absolute counts vs error rate, hangs, queue/backlog depth, and saturation. Then check whether any downstream or sibling service shows elevated errors/latency or timeouts in the same window. Report: symptom onset timestamp, which services actually deviate from baseline, and the error/timeout signatures.

Find what changed and when across ALL services (not only payment-service): list deployments, config changes, and feature-flag/credential/network changes in the window ~2026-04-02T09:00Z to 13:59Z that touch payment-service or anything it depends on. Map payment-service's service dependencies (upstream callers, downstream bank/PSP connector, ledger, auth, gateway, shared components) and identify any shared component that many services rely on. Also search historical incidents for precedents: prior cases where 'customers report payment failures but payment-service error rate is normal'.

Correlate the root cause: taking the onset time and affected-service list from task a, check which of the changes found in task b occurred at or just before onset and aligns with the affected blast radius. Explicitly test the reporter's suspicion (client app / bank side vs server-side): determine whether the pattern is consistent with an external-only cause or whether an internal change/dependency explains it. Report the most likely culprit, the evidence for/against each theory, and any confirming signal observable should check.

args.query: customers report payment failures but payment-service error rate normal

events.statement: Only one deployment occurred across all services in the 09:00–13:59Z window: settlement-service v1.9.0 (dep-5510) at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z, summary 'Batch settlement report export' / 'new CSV exporter', status live with rolled_back_at null. No payment-service deployment exists in this window.

Exactly one config change in the window: payment-service cfg-2502 changed bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair, described as 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'.

payment-service direct dependency edges: -> ledger-db (db), -> bank-partner-api (external), -> kafka (queue-produce); inbound: api-gateway -> payment-service (http). bank-partner-api is type external, owner vendor, has_telemetry:false.
Two shared components are in payment-service's graph and are shared=true: ledger-db (postgres) and kafka — the note states "'shared' datastores are used by several services".

ledger-db is written by four services (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service) and kafka is produced/consumed by four services (order-service, payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service) — so both are cross-team fan-in points that could affect payment-service from outside.

Historical precedents matching 'payment failures without payment-service errors': HIST-105 (2025-11-19) 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage' on payment-service, root cause 'Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes (their incident)', category dependency_failure, match_score 2 — the only exact symptom match. Related leads: HIST-106 (settlement mTLS certificate expired) and HIST-111 (reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db, services ledger-db+settlement-service).

Timeline alignment: the settlement-service deploy (10:30Z) and the payment-service bank timeout config change (11:20Z) both precede the 12:32Z report, and the config change is explicitly connected to a 'partner advisory' about the bank API; the timeout was raised (3s→5s), not lowered or rolled back.

events.description: No telemetry query was run against bank-partner-api or payment-service metric series to confirm whether calls to the partner degraded; bank-partner-api itself has_telemetry:false, so its own health cannot be measured directly (tc-003).

Search returned only 6 historical incidents (limit 6) and the result was not flagged truncated, but no further precedents were explored, e.g. credential-expiry or config-change cases specific to payment-service.

No queries were made for network changes, feature-flag flips, or credential/secret rotations in the 09:00–13:59Z window (only get_config_changes and get_deployments were available and returned 1 each); absence of flag/credential changes is therefore unverified rather than proven absent.

events.answer: In the 09:00–13:59Z window only two changes exist: a settlement-service deploy (dep-5510, v1.9.0, new CSV exporter, 10:30Z, still live, not rolled back) and a payment-service config change (cfg-2502, bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000, 11:20Z, by p.nair, "after partner advisory"). payment-service itself had no deployments. payment-service depends on shared components ledger-db and kafka (both shared=true), plus api-gateway upstream and the un-telemetered external bank-partner-api downstream. Historical precedent HIST-105 (2025-11-19, "Payment failures: bank partner API outage") matches the symptom pattern of payment failures with a partner-side cause.

events.statement: payment-service's bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 100% at 12:14Z (bucket 12:14 avg=50.1, max=100) and stayed at 100% through 12:30Z, versus a flat ~0.20% baseline from 11:00-12:12Z.
payment-service's payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5%: 12:12Z avg=38.93, then 12:20Z avg=2.72 / max=3.3, and remained ~2.1-2.7% through 13:56Z (summary min 1.44, mean 42.74).

payment-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stayed flat at baseline the entire window: avg 0.19-0.27%, max 0.32% from 11:00 through 13:56Z, with no deviation at the 12:12-12:28 onset buckets (avg 0.23 / 0.19 / 0.24).

payment-service logs show the failure signature is an expired client certificate at the bank boundary: 80x 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (first 12:16:44Z) and 54x 'marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (first 12:15:27Z).

A cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z pre-dated the failure: 'client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z)'; a single 'retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset' WARN appeared at 12:04:22Z, before the 12:15 expiry.

payment-service request_rate and latency_p99_ms show no overload signature: request_rate held steady ~90-110 req/s across the incident (mean 100.21), and p99 latency actually DROPPED from ~320ms baseline to ~138-144ms after 12:20Z, consistent with failed calls short-circuiting rather than hanging.

bank-partner-api has no directly observable telemetry: querying it returns not_found with 'this is an external dependency: we have no logs/metrics for it. Observe it through its callers.' So the bank side can only be assessed via payment-service's bank_api_error_rate.

events.description: Could not query sibling/caller services (e.g. api-gateway, other services calling payment-service) or bank-partner-api logs: the api-gateway log query and further log queries returned budget_exhausted.
bank-partner-api exposes no metrics/logs (external dependency, not_found); its own error rate and cert state are not directly observable.

Did not retrieve payment-service timeout counts, queue/backlog depth, db_pool_in_use, cpu_pct/memory_pct, or restarts before the budget was exhausted; only latency_p99, request_rate, error_rate, bank_api_error_rate, payment_success_rate were pulled.

events.answer: The payment failures are REAL but are being masked from the HTTP error-rate panel: at 12:14-12:15Z payment-service's bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 100% and payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.3%, while error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stayed flat at ~0.2%. Signature: mTLS/TLS failure to the external bank-partner-api because payment-service's own client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 12:15:00Z. Failed payments are converted to PENDING_RETRY (not 5xx), so the dashboard looks green. Onset of customer-visible failure ≈ 12:14-12:15Z, not 11:45-12:30.

events.statement: Re-queried all-services changes for 09:00-13:59Z: exactly one config change (cfg-2502, payment-service, bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000, 11:20:00Z, p.nair) and one deployment (dep-5510, settlement-service v1.9.0, 10:30:00Z). No certificate/credential/secret change or payment-service deployment appears anywhere in the window.

Change-to-onset alignment: the latest change before onset is cfg-2502 at 11:20Z, ~54-55 minutes BEFORE the 12:14-12:15Z onset; the settlement deploy is ~104 min before. Neither is at or just before onset, so no internal change aligns tightly with the failure onset.

Reporter's external-only theory is contradicted at the boundary description but not fully: payment-service's failure is at its OWN client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), i.e. an expired credential on the CLIENT side of the mTLS handshake, not a bank-side 5xx. HIST-105 (external bank 5xx) does NOT match; HIST-106 (settlement mTLS certificate expired, credential_expiry, higher match_score 4) is the closer precedent.

cfg-2502 is a timeout INCREASE (3000->5000ms) justified by a 'partner advisory', not a credential rotation. It can only mask hangs (make calls wait longer), and T1's F13 shows latency actually DROPPED, so this change is not the failure mechanism; at most it is unrelated context (a partner advisory predating the cert expiry).

External-only cause cannot be confirmed from outside: bank-partner-api has no telemetry (has_telemetry:false, type external), so no independent signal exists to attribute the failure to the bank. The only evidence localizes the failure to payment-service's client cert.

events.description: No certificate/credential/secret lifecycle change appears in the 09:00-13:59Z config/deploy feeds, so the mechanism by which the client cert reached expiry (no renewal, alert ignored) is not visible in the change record; only the cert-watcher WARN at 11:50Z (F12) hints at it.
bank-partner-api exposes no logs/metrics (has_telemetry:false), so I cannot independently test whether the bank side was healthy concurrently.

No config/deploy change occurred at or just before the 12:14-12:15Z onset, so an internal-change-triggered mechanism is ruled out but the true trigger (time-based cert expiry) is not a 'change' event in these feeds.

events.answer: No internal change aligns with the onset: the only payment-service-adjacent change (cfg-2502, bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000ms) happened at 11:20Z, ~55 min before the 12:14-12:15Z failure onset, and is a timeout increase (not a credential change), while the only deployment (settlement-service v1.9.0, 10:30Z) is ~104 min before onset and unrelated. The reporter's external-only / 'bank side' theory is not supported: the failure is an mTLS client-certificate expiry on payment-service's own side (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), matching historical precedent HIST-106 (expired mTLS cert), not HIST-105 (bank 5xx). Most likely culprit: payment-service's own expired client certificate at the bank boundary — an internal credential-lifecycle failure, not a client-app or bank-side outage; but no change record explains it because expiry is time-based, so it must be confirmed via payment-service logs/cert-watcher.

tasks.objective: Establish whether the payment failures are real and where. Determine the onset time of customer-visible failure (look for incident-like signals ~11:45-12:30Z, ~40 tickets in the last ~15 min before 12:32). Check payment-service's full metric set, not just error_rate: latency percentiles (p95/p99), timeout counts, request rate/absolute counts vs error rate, hangs, queue/backlog depth, and saturation. Then check whether any downstream or sibling service shows elevated errors/latency or timeouts in the same window. Report: symptom onset timestamp, which services actually deviate from baseline, and the error/timeout signatures.
tasks.answer: The payment failures are REAL but are being masked from the HTTP error-rate panel: at 12:14-12:15Z payment-service's bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 100% and payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.3%, while error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stayed flat at ~0.2%. Signature: mTLS/TLS failure to the external bank-partner-api because payment-service's own client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired at 12:15:00Z. Failed payments are converted to PENDING_RETRY (not 5xx), so the dashboard looks green. Onset of customer-visible failure ≈ 12:14-12:15Z, not 11:45-12:30.

tasks.objective: Find what changed and when across ALL services (not only payment-service): list deployments, config changes, and feature-flag/credential/network changes in the window ~2026-04-02T09:00Z to 13:59Z that touch payment-service or anything it depends on. Map payment-service's service dependencies (upstream callers, downstream bank/PSP connector, ledger, auth, gateway, shared components) and identify any shared component that many services rely on. Also search historical incidents for precedents: prior cases where 'customers report payment failures but payment-service error rate is normal'.
tasks.answer: In the 09:00–13:59Z window only two changes exist: a settlement-service deploy (dep-5510, v1.9.0, new CSV exporter, 10:30Z, still live, not rolled back) and a payment-service config change (cfg-2502, bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000, 11:20Z, by p.nair, "after partner advisory"). payment-service itself had no deployments. payment-service depends on shared components ledger-db and kafka (both shared=true), plus api-gateway upstream and the un-telemetered external bank-partner-api downstream. Historical precedent HIST-105 (2025-11-19, "Payment failures: bank partner API outage") matches the symptom pattern of payment failures with a partner-side cause.

tasks.objective: Correlate the root cause: taking the onset time and affected-service list from task a, check which of the changes found in task b occurred at or just before onset and aligns with the affected blast radius. Explicitly test the reporter's suspicion (client app / bank side vs server-side): determine whether the pattern is consistent with an external-only cause or whether an internal change/dependency explains it. Report the most likely culprit, the evidence for/against each theory, and any confirming signal observable should check.
tasks.answer: No internal change aligns with the onset: the only payment-service-adjacent change (cfg-2502, bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000ms) happened at 11:20Z, ~55 min before the 12:14-12:15Z failure onset, and is a timeout increase (not a credential change), while the only deployment (settlement-service v1.9.0, 10:30Z) is ~104 min before onset and unrelated. The reporter's external-only / 'bank side' theory is not supported: the failure is an mTLS client-certificate expiry on payment-service's own side (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), matching historical precedent HIST-106 (expired mTLS cert), not HIST-105 (bank 5xx). Most likely culprit: payment-service's own expired client certificate at the bank boundary — an internal credential-lifecycle failure, not a client-app or bank-side outage; but no change record explains it because expiry is time-based, so it must be confirmed via payment-service logs/cert-watcher.
